input.question: A developer creates a new test file at `frontend/test/metabase/lib/analytics.test.ts` to test analytics utilities in the Metabase frontend. After running the Jest test suite, they notice none of the tests in that file were executed. What is the most likely reason?

options.A: The Jest configuration's `testMatch` patterns only match files ending in `.unit.spec.{js,jsx,ts,tsx}`, so a file named `analytics.test.ts` is never discovered by the test runner.
options.B: TypeScript test files must be compiled to JavaScript before Jest can run them; a `.ts` file without a prior build step is silently skipped.
options.C: The file must be co-located with the source file it tests (i.e., next to `analytics.ts`) rather than placed in a separate `test/` directory.
options.D: Test files placed under `frontend/test/` are excluded by `testPathIgnorePatterns`, so only files under `frontend/src/` are executed.
